deckTitle: What Work Was For: A Field Report from Before the Timesheet — Vol. I

cards.power: Generates raw survival.
cards.lore: The bend worn into the earth over generations.
cards.gradeReason: Badger digs. You dig. No explanation required. Pure pre-historical work embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark watercolor. Subject: badger clawing earth at dusk near ancient trail groove. Mood: urgent, ancestral.

cards.power: Sorts the pack by utility.
cards.lore: The bad knee guards the young; the keen eye takes the high branches.
cards.gradeReason: Owl on branch, wolf sprinting. Clear specialisation metaphor but evolution frame needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: naturalist watercolor. Subject: owl perched high, wolf running below in twilight forest. Mood: efficient, hierarchical.

cards.power: Distributes daylight evenly.
cards.lore: The day ended when there was enough.
cards.gradeReason: Bears hauling log at sunset. Collective labor, natural end condition — you feel it instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: warm watercolor. Subject: three bears carrying massive log toward setting sun. Mood: communal, sufficient.

cards.power: Detaches repetition from appetite.
cards.lore: The moment "doing" became "duty".
cards.gradeReason: Beaver gnawing with modern dam behind. The historical twist from instinct to obligation needs unpacking.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sepia watercolor. Subject: beaver gnawing branch, modern concrete dam looming behind. Mood: transitional, melancholy.

cards.power: Creates the concept of laziness.
cards.lore: The small gap between bending out of hunger and bending out of habit.
cards.gradeReason: Cat asleep in gears. Laziness only exists once duty does. Instant conceptual crystallization.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: steampunk watercolor. Subject: fat cat napping in giant industrial gear teeth. Mood: smug, defiant, invented.

cards.power: Slices the sun into eight prayers.
cards.lore: The day has owners, and they are calling.
cards.gradeReason: Goat flung by enormous bell. You feel the day being seized. G1 sensory violence.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medieval illuminated watercolor. Subject: startled goat airborne from giant bronze bell explosion. Mood: commanding, disorienting.

cards.power: Transforms prayer into industrial shifts.
cards.lore: Time is now currency; it is spent, not passed.
cards.gradeReason: Crow screaming smoke over factory stacks. Industrial era frame helps connect bell-to-whistle arc.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark industrial watercolor. Subject: black crow shrieking beside belching factory smokestacks at dawn. Mood: coercive, mechanical.

cards.power: Consumes all available existence.
cards.lore: Daylight is the only legitimate limit to availability.
cards.gradeReason: Skeleton horse hauling rocks under full moon. Pre-labor-law horror — total depletion made flesh.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gothic watercolor. Subject: skeletal horse pulling overloaded cart under enormous full moon. Mood: exhausted, merciless.

cards.power: Reclaims exactly eight hours for "what we will."
cards.lore: A radical claim that some time belongs to the breather.
cards.gradeReason: Raccoon with '3x8' banner in crowd. Eight-hour movement energy immediate. You want to chant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: agitprop watercolor. Subject: raccoon on podium waving '3x8' placard before rally crowd. Mood: defiant, triumphant.

cards.power: Fractures fluid movement into cold math.
cards.lore: The future belongs to the system; the past belonged to the beast.
cards.gradeReason: Squirrel smashing enormous pocket watch. Taylor's scientific management lurks but name doesn't appear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: kinetic watercolor. Subject: panicked squirrel wrestling with exploding stopwatch, gears flying. Mood: fragmented, violent.

cards.power: Quadruples the load bearing capacity of flesh.
cards.lore: The first manual for treating the body as a gear.
cards.gradeReason: Bull wearing stacked anvils. Taylorist body-as-machine concept needs the era context to land fully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: industrial watercolor. Subject: muscular bull strapped with piled anvils straining forward. Mood: brutal, efficient, commodified.

cards.power: Multiplies output by a factor of 240.
cards.lore: Making things without knowing how to make a thing.
cards.gradeReason: Mice at machines cutting and reeling. Smith's pin factory reference brilliant but educational frame helps.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dickensian watercolor. Subject: three mice at separate factory machines making wire and cutting pins. Mood: mindless, mechanized.

cards.power: Severs the maker from the whole.
cards.lore: Ten beasts make forty-eight thousand fragments.
cards.gradeReason: Animal assembly line holding different tools. Marxist alienation subtext enriches but isn't required.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: allegory watercolor. Subject: line of different animals each holding one specialist tool in row. Mood: fragmented, productive, hollow.

cards.power: Enriches the system by impoverishing the soul.
cards.lore: The worker grows poorer the more wealth they produce.
cards.gradeReason: Sheep shearing itself into industrial vacuum. Marx's estranged labour in one image — brilliant but needs the frame.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surreal watercolor. Subject: sheep shearing its own wool, sucked immediately into factory vacuum pipe. Mood: absurd, tragic.

cards.power: Extracts the ghost from the machine.
cards.lore: The factory starves if the worker keeps what they make.
cards.gradeReason: Top-hatted pig siphoning liquid from tiny mice workers. Surplus value made grotesque — context makes it devastating.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: political cartoon watercolor. Subject: fat pig in top hat drinking from tubes connected to exhausted mice workers. Mood: parasitic, grotesque.

cards.power: Forces the calling into inescapable logic.
cards.lore: No one can leave without ceasing to be modern.
cards.gradeReason: Bird outside/inside steel cube with padlock. Weber's 'iron cage' image is clean but name does heavy lifting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: austere watercolor. Subject: small colorful bird standing beside padlocked steel-framed cube, identical twin inside. Mood: trapped, inevitable.

cards.power: Puts life on a shelf with a price tag.
cards.lore: Land, coin, and sweat become goods.
cards.gradeReason: Cow with barcode on store shelf. Price-tag labour is legible but commodity fetish frame gives depth.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: supermarket satire watercolor. Subject: docile cow lying on price-tagged supermarket shelf with barcode on flank. Mood: degrading, matter-of-fact.

cards.power: Trades the part of the self that fills the time.
cards.lore: The person becomes the meat inside the hour.
cards.gradeReason: Fox receiving swirling coin for intangible spiral. Self-as-commodity resonates but labour-time frame enriches it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: symbolic watercolor. Subject: fox receiving spinning gold coin in exchange for glowing swirl of energy. Mood: transactional, eerie.

cards.power: Liberates the thinker from the typing pool.
cards.lore: An invention designed to free you, destined to cage you.
cards.gradeReason: Frog architect sketching blueprints. Herman Miller's 1960s promise vs. cubicle result. Historical context amplifies.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: mid-century watercolor. Subject: cheerful frog at drafting desk sketching open-plan layout, cubicle maze behind. Mood: ironic, idealistic.

cards.power: Shrinks the horizon to modular plastic.
cards.lore: A revolution mass-produced into a prison.
cards.gradeReason: Deer heads poking over grey cubicle walls, eyes wide. Every office worker recognizes this without a single word.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: fluorescent office watercolor. Subject: several stunned deer heads visible above identical grey cubicle partitions. Mood: caged, institutionalized.

cards.power: Deploys the mind as the means of production.
cards.lore: Cannot be coerced; must be persuaded, motivated, included.
cards.gradeReason: Owl with exposed brain held like a machine part. Mind-as-factory-floor. You ARE the instrument of production.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: anatomical watercolor. Subject: stern owl in collar holding up its own glowing brain surrounded by equations. Mood: analytical, extracted.

cards.power: Replaces the physical whip with administrative paper.
cards.lore: The illusion of dignity, infinitely measurable.
cards.gradeReason: Rabbit buried under avalanche of memos. The paper whip is felt universally. Zero frame needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: chaotic office watercolor. Subject: panicked rabbit drowning under exploding pile of administrative memos and forms. Mood: overwhelmed, Kafkaesque.

cards.power: Replaces the assembly belt with a conference table.
cards.lore: Where time goes to be collectively sacrificed.
cards.gradeReason: Fish heads in suits at conference table staring at blank screen. Every worker's lived nightmare, zero frame needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corporate watercolor. Subject: blank-faced fish in suits seated around conference table, blank projection screen. Mood: vacant, performative.

cards.power: Expands work to fill the allotted void.
cards.lore: It takes six weeks because six weeks were given.
cards.gradeReason: Enormous bloated toad filling the frame. Parkinson's Law in animal form — brilliant if you know the name.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: absurdist watercolor. Subject: obese toad expanding to fill entire room, smug expression, files scattered. Mood: bloated, inevitable.

cards.power: Warps reality into three-month chunks.
cards.lore: The beast shapes itself to please the analyst.
cards.gradeReason: Hamster in spinning pie-chart wheel. Every corporate creature recognizes the Q4 sprint trap instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corporate satire watercolor. Subject: panicked hamster running in wheel shaped like quarterly pie chart. Mood: frantic, cyclical.

cards.power: Destroys the underlying value of any measurement.
cards.lore: When a measure becomes a target, truth dies.
cards.gradeReason: Dog racing off a cliff chasing robot rabbit. Visually striking but 'Goodhart' as a name does heavy lifting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: chase watercolor. Subject: dog sprinting off cliff edge chasing mechanical rabbit decoy. Mood: blind, self-defeating.

cards.power: Tells a comforting fiction about how power flows.
cards.lore: The real currents are sideways and in the shadows.
cards.gradeReason: Spider web labelled CEO/VP/MANAGER with spider below. Web-as-org-chart is clever but irony needs the read.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gothic bureaucratic watercolor. Subject: elaborate spider web on chalkboard labelled with org chart titles, spider waiting below. Mood: conspiratorial, false.

cards.power: Shuffles the deck while the dealer cheats.
cards.lore: A periodic ritual to pretend the river changed course.
cards.gradeReason: Giant hand shaking snow globe of panicking ant-workers. God-mode corporate indifference. Perfectly G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surreal watercolor. Subject: enormous hand shaking snow globe containing tiny ant workers at office desks. Mood: arbitrary, powerless.

cards.power: Forces mutual dishonesty once a year.
cards.lore: Most reviews are dishonest in both directions.
cards.gradeReason: Snake wearing smiley mask reviews rat also masked. Bilateral dishonesty in one image. Devastatingly G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark satire watercolor. Subject: snake in suit wearing smiling mask reviews rat across table, rat also masked. Mood: mutual, performative, absurd.

cards.power: Dooms a percentage of the pack before they begin.
cards.lore: The line was drawn before you entered the room.
cards.gradeReason: Crow with scythe tossing 'Bottom 10%' papers in bin. Forced ranking system legible but jargon helps.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bureaucratic watercolor. Subject: crow with scythe throwing 'Bottom 10%' files into trash can, bar chart behind. Mood: predetermined, ruthless.

cards.power: Verifies the existence of a corporate lie.
cards.lore: Writing the report no one will ever read.
cards.gradeReason: Parrot in suit stamping APPROVED on endless paper stack. Bureaucratic futility clear but Graeber's framing sharpens it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: office satire watercolor. Subject: parrot in tie stamping enormous stack of forms with APPROVED stamp. Mood: mindless, infinite.

cards.power: Patches a glitch that should not exist.
cards.lore: Human glue for digital incompetence.
cards.gradeReason: Octopus holding broken industrial pipes together. 'Human glue for digital incompetence' needs the Graeber taxonomy to click.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: industrial watercolor. Subject: octopus using all eight arms to hold leaking industrial pipes together. Mood: desperate, systemic.

cards.power: Manages the unmanageable for no reason.
cards.lore: Supervising those who already know what to do.
cards.gradeReason: Sloth in a suit pointing a stick at a working beehive. The archetype is complete. Instantly playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corporate satire watercolor. Subject: slow sloth in business suit gesturing vaguely at busy beehive with pointer stick. Mood: superfluous, pompous.

cards.power: Magnifies the ego of the superior.
cards.lore: Existing solely to make someone else look important.
cards.gradeReason: Full-display peacock next to humble pigeon with briefcase. Social function of flunky crystallized without one word of explanation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: status watercolor. Subject: full-fan peacock standing beside small grey pigeon carrying briefcase looking deflated. Mood: performative, hierarchy.

cards.power: Counters the enemy's identical minion.
cards.lore: The arms race of corporate lawyers and lobbyists.
cards.gradeReason: Two armored rhinos facing off in marble hall. Mutual deterrence archetype — no explanation needed, pure G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: feudal corporate watercolor. Subject: two armored rhinoceroses facing each other in corporate marble lobby. Mood: adversarial, mirrored.

cards.power: Translates feudal advancement into cubicles.
cards.lore: The modern firm calls it seniority; the guild called it survival.
cards.gradeReason: Giraffe in transparent glass ceiling office. The feudal-to-corporate translation is sharp but needs the dual frame.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: glass tower watercolor. Subject: giraffe neck stretched through glass office ceiling, looking at leaf on desk above. Mood: striving, surreal.

cards.power: Merges the core self with the corporate role.
cards.lore: When asked who you are, you answer what you do.
cards.gradeReason: Chameleon staring at blank HELLO MY NAME IS screen. Identity merger is there but requires a beat of thought.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: identity crisis watercolor. Subject: chameleon before glowing monitor displaying blank name tag, skin shifting grey. Mood: merged, hollow.

cards.power: Exploits itself without external pressure.
cards.lore: The push is internal; the push is the air you breathe.
cards.gradeReason: Greyhound holding its own leash while sprinting. Han's achievement-subject in one perfect image. G1 peak of the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: burnout watercolor. Subject: racing greyhound gripping its own leash in its mouth, sprinting through flames. Mood: self-driven, inescapable.

cards.power: Consumes the self from the inside out.
cards.lore: You cannot stop being the one who runs.
cards.gradeReason: 'World's Best Boss' mug in charred hand from ash-heap office chair. Entire burnout culture in one devastating image.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: scorched watercolor. Subject: charred remains in office chair, intact 'World's Best Boss' mug in carbonized hand. Mood: obliterated, ironic.

cards.power: Turns the passage of time into physical agony.
cards.lore: Alienation felt in the bone, not the book.
cards.gradeReason: Elephant with clocks crashing around it. Time-as-physical-weight concept emotionally clear but needs the burnout frame.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surreal watercolor. Subject: exhausted elephant surrounded by falling grandfather clocks in storm-grey air. Mood: crushing, temporal.

cards.power: Defeats the hermeneutics of suspicion.
cards.lore: The carburettor answers you in a way the spreadsheet never will.
cards.gradeReason: 'Hermeneutics of suspicion' in Power text is a real jargon wall. Sennett reference loses non-academics instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: workshop watercolor. Subject: badger with wrench repairing old engine in candlelit garage, gears gleaming. Mood: absorbed, honest.

cards.power: Remembers what the mind was trained to forget.
cards.lore: The body knows the whole object.
cards.gradeReason: Raccoon weaving in darkness. Tactile knowledge contra abstraction felt but the framing edge is in the lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: intimate watercolor. Subject: raccoon in candlelight weaving wicker basket, focused, no phone nearby. Mood: embodied, quiet.

cards.power: Cares for the work strictly for its own sake.
cards.lore: A slowness the modern firm cannot tolerate.
cards.gradeReason: Turtle carving ornate wooden box. Speed-as-value critique needs the productivity-culture contrast to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: artisan watercolor. Subject: ancient turtle carefully chiselling ornate floral pattern into dark wood box. Mood: slow, purposeful.

cards.power: Replaces mastery with a slide deck.
cards.lore: We no longer apprentice; we are processed.
cards.gradeReason: Ducklings on conveyor belt toward screen labelled 'Buzz words'. Processed vs. apprenticed is clear with context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: industrial satire watercolor. Subject: line of identical ducklings on conveyor belt moving toward corporate training screen. Mood: processed, compliant.

cards.power: Delivers exactly what is paid for, no more.
cards.lore: The structural refusal to gift the surplus.
cards.gradeReason: Cat at desk, pen untouched, coffee untouched. Culturally loaded term meets perfect embodiment. Pure G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: office realism watercolor. Subject: cat at computer desk, pen down, expression serene and unmoved, mug untouched. Mood: minimum viable, sovereign.

cards.power: Denies the system its desires.
cards.lore: Only by doing nothing can you be the measure of all things.
cards.gradeReason: Panda flat on floor ignoring ringing phone. Tang ping movement rendered instantly performable. G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: zen refusal watercolor. Subject: panda lying completely flat on floor, vintage phone ringing nearby, ignored. Mood: deliberate, sovereign.

cards.power: Harbours the work that actually matters.
cards.lore: The sanctuary of the un-alienated soul.
cards.gradeReason: Mole in crystal underground cave beneath grey factory. The real work lives underground. Immediately felt.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: magical underground watercolor. Subject: mole in glowing crystal cave beneath grey factory, sketching with joy. Mood: liberated, hidden, real.

cards.power: Promises a leisure that never arrives.
cards.lore: The productivity went somewhere, but it didn't come back to you.
cards.gradeReason: Ghost owl with floating clocks and numbers. Keynes' 15-hour week prediction is unspoken reference — too abstract alone.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ghostly watercolor. Subject: translucent owl in top hat surrounded by floating clock faces and scattered numbers. Mood: spectral, promised, absent.

cards.power: Erases the boundary between dusk and dawn.
cards.lore: The Bed and the Desk have merged.
cards.gradeReason: Snake coiled around glowing phone in bed pillow. The surveillance-capitalism bedroom invasion — nobody needs this explained.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: nocturnal watercolor. Subject: snake in serpentine coil around glowing phone resting on bedroom pillow at night. Mood: invasive, inescapable.

cards.power: Invades the sanctuary of the mind at 11:47 PM.
cards.lore: The structural unit of the new, endless workday.
cards.gradeReason: Neon blue wasps invading hibernating bear's cave at night. Invasive ambient work ping — visceral and universal G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bioluminescent watercolor. Subject: electric blue wasps swarming into dark cave toward sleeping bear, clocks on cave wall. Mood: violated, anxious.

cards.power: Camouflages the office in domestic cloth.
cards.lore: A costume the office did not know it was getting.
cards.gradeReason: Chained sheep in pyjamas at kitchen laptop with padlock collar. Post-COVID home-office trap embodied perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: domestic horror watercolor. Subject: sheep in pyjamas chained by padlock to kitchen desk with open laptop. Mood: cozy-coercive, trapped.

cards.power: Engineers recovery strictly to fuel more labor.
cards.lore: You rest only to return to the work in better shape.
cards.gradeReason: Iguana in Hawaiian shirt on beach, laptop open. The vacation that isn't — modern workers live this scene.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tropical satire watercolor. Subject: iguana in Hawaiian shirt working on laptop at beach, palm trees, waves. Mood: exhausted, colonized.

cards.power: Waits patiently to inherit your function.
cards.lore: The replacement does not need a quarterly report.
cards.gradeReason: Robot arm in spotlight, patient and precise. AI-replacement anxiety is real but needs 'your function' frame to sting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: industrial spotlight watercolor. Subject: robotic arm lit by spotlight in empty factory, human tools gathering dust. Mood: inevitable, patient.

cards.power: Manifests the shame of our own slowness.
cards.lore: Surpassed by our own products, smaller than ourselves.
cards.gradeReason: Sad bloodhound watching machines through factory window. Serling-pathos resonant but richer with the Twilight Zone reference.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: twilight zone watercolor. Subject: melancholy hound pressed against factory window watching automated machinery work inside. Mood: bereft, superseded.

cards.power: Sits quietly where the worker used to stand.
cards.lore: The machine that no longer needs us.
cards.gradeReason: Overgrown hammer and axe reclaimed by moss and flowers. Poetic image needs the 'worker used to stand here' contrast.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: nature reclaiming watercolor. Subject: abandoned hammer and axe covered in moss, wildflowers growing through handle, spiderwebs. Mood: forgotten, ecological.

cards.power: Reclaims contemplation and festival.
cards.lore: The part of the day that has no purpose outside itself.
cards.gradeReason: Animals dancing at bonfire — fox, badger, rabbit, owl. Entire pre-industrial deck returns to celebrate. Perfect G1 close.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: celebratory watercolor. Subject: badger, fox, rabbit, owl dancing joyfully around blazing bonfire under stars. Mood: liberated, complete, alive.

verdict: Field report approved, and it's the best version of this deck yet. The 14-part arc is structurally airtight — survival, ownership, measurement, bullshit archetypes, burnout, craftsman ghost, broken contract, ambient factory, final obsolescence, bonfire — turning 56 cards into a readable essay with chapter headings. 'The Achievement-Subject,' 'The Burned,' and 'The Reorg' are all-time KFB cards. The only soft territory is Part XI, where 'Defeats the hermeneutics of suspicion' in The Mended Thing's Power field drops non-Sennett readers cold. WEB_v1 polish is clear: zero font artifacts, clean layout, consistent comic-spread feel. Table-ready Y.
blurb: For anyone who ever answered 'What do you do?' and felt something leave the body. A 56-card field report on work from badger-era survival to AI replacement — Vol. I.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — FrizzleBob panic-frozen in EXIT-sign office cave, clocks at 8:00, filing cabinets as walls — one image says everything
coverQA.coverTitle: 4 — 'What Work Was For: A Field Report from Before the Timesheet' is brilliant but long; reads fine at deck scale
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Bullshit Jobs + field-report + Vol. I framing all land simultaneously, exactly the tone inside
coverQA.coverOriginality: 5 — The institutional dungeon with EXIT as the only signage is a new visual frame for this universe
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — Strong scroll-stopper; 'A Field Report from Before the Timesheet' is a shareable tagline
coverQA.coverNote: Strongest cover in the What Work Was For series — FrizzleBob trapped between IN/OUT board and EXIT sign is the deck's thesis in one panel. Coffee stain is a nice physical detail. Full marks on vibe match.

notes: Polished Gumroad WEB_v1 release. 14 named Parts with subtitle captions above each spread — this structural device is new and excellent, turning the 56-card deck into a readable essay. No RAF dice boxes. 'BLÖDSINN!', 'KayfaBOGGLE!', 'KayfaBINGO!' interjections appear in margins on several pages — consistent KFB visual language. Subtitle captions act as chapter headings and dramatically increase educational coherence. Gumroad ID watermark on p.1 only. Distinct from older 'What_Work_Was_For - ADD web ID.pdf' prototypes.

quickWins: Simplify 'Defeats the hermeneutics of suspicion' in The Mended Thing's Power field — or move it to notes
niceToHave: The Fifteen-Hour Illusion could name Keynes explicitly in lore for the educated-audience edition
